lessons.title: How Am I Feeling Today?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to name a basic feeling (happy, sad, cross, worried) and match it to a face.
lessons.starter_activity: Sing 'If You're Happy and You Know It' with actions on the carpet.
lessons.main_activity: Introduce feelings-face cards. Model naming your own feeling today. Children take turns picking a face card and saying how they feel, supported by an adult sentence starter: 'Today I feel ___ because ___.'
key_questions: How do you feel this morning?
What does a happy face look like? A sad face?
What could we do if a friend feels sad?

differentiation.support: Use only 2 contrasting faces (happy/sad) with 1:1 adult modelling
differentiation.extension: Ask child to suggest why a puppet character might feel a certain way in a short scenario

lessons.assessment_notes: Note which children can independently name a feeling vs. need visual prompting; record on Learning Journey under PSED.1.
lessons.plenary: Each child places their name peg next to today's feeling on the class 'Feelings Wall'.
lessons.home_link: Ask your child to tell you one thing that made them feel happy today.

lessons.title: Listening Games: Whose Voice Is It?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to listen attentively and identify a familiar voice/sound without looking.
lessons.starter_activity: Play 'Freeze' — children move to music and freeze in silence when it stops.
lessons.main_activity: Children sit in a circle with eyes closed; adult chooses a child to say 'good morning' in a disguised voice; others guess who it is. Follow with a simple instruction-following game ('touch your nose, then clap twice').
key_questions: How did you know it was that voice?
What two things did I ask you to do?

differentiation.support: Give one-step instructions only
differentiation.extension: Give three-step instructions in sequence

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe who follows 2-step vs 1-step instructions accurately — evidence for CL.1.
lessons.plenary: Recap: 'What do good listeners do with their eyes, ears and mouth?'
lessons.home_link: Play 'Simon Says' at home with 2-step instructions.

lessons.title: Moving Safely Around Our New Classroom
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to move around a space avoiding obstacles and each other.
lessons.starter_activity: Warm-up stretches to music.
lessons.main_activity: Set out cones/hoops as obstacles in the hall. Children practise walking, then jogging, around them on a 'traffic light' stop/go signal from the teacher.
key_questions: How do we keep our bodies safe when we move?
What happens if we bump into a friend?

differentiation.support: Reduce number of obstacles, walk only
differentiation.extension: Add jogging and changing direction on signal

lessons.assessment_notes: Note spatial awareness and control — evidence for PD.1 gross motor.
lessons.plenary: Cool-down breathing exercise; children say one rule for moving safely.
lessons.home_link: Practise walking around furniture at home without touching it.

lessons.title: Phonics: Introducing 's'
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to say the sound 's' and identify objects that start with it.
lessons.starter_activity: Sing the phonics warm-up song for the day's sound.
lessons.main_activity: Introduce the grapheme 's' using an action/mnemonic (e.g. 'slither like a snake, sss'). Children practise the sound, then sort picture cards into 's' / 'not s'.
key_questions: Can you think of a word that starts with 'sss'?
What does your mouth do when you say 'sss'?

differentiation.support: Focus on oral sound only, no writing
differentiation.extension: Attempt to write 's' in the sand tray

lessons.assessment_notes: Track individual phonics tracker: can the child produce the sound on sight of the grapheme?
lessons.plenary: Class recap of the sound with actions.
lessons.home_link: Spot 3 things at home that start with the 's' sound.

lessons.title: Counting Ourselves: How Many Children Today?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to count a small group of objects/people up to 10, touching each once.
lessons.starter_activity: Count children on the carpet together as a group chant to 10.
lessons.main_activity: In small groups, children count sets of counters/toys (up to 5, then up to 10 for confident counters), touching each item as they count.
key_questions: How many are there?
Is that more or less than mine?
What happens if we add one more?

differentiation.support: Count to 5 with 1:1 adult support and physical touch-counting
differentiation.extension: Count to 10+ and compare two sets

lessons.assessment_notes: Record highest number counted accurately with 1:1 correspondence — evidence for MATHS.1.
lessons.plenary: Count down from 10 to 0 together like a rocket launch.
lessons.home_link: Count stairs, spoons, or toys together at home.

lessons.title: Our New Classroom and School
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to name key areas of the classroom/school and their purpose.
lessons.starter_activity: Walk around the classroom pointing out and naming key areas.
lessons.main_activity: Guided tour of the school (hall, toilets, playground, office). Children draw or point to their favourite area on a simple school map.
key_questions: Where do we go if we feel unwell?
Where do we play outside?

differentiation.support: Focus on 2-3 key areas only (classroom, toilet, playground)
differentiation.extension: Sequence the school tour in order using photos

lessons.assessment_notes: Note recall of school layout after a few days — evidence for UTW.2.
lessons.plenary: Children share which area they liked best and why.
lessons.home_link: Draw a picture of your classroom to bring in and talk about.

lessons.title: Self-Portrait Collage
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to use materials purposefully to represent their own face.
lessons.starter_activity: Look in mirrors and describe own facial features to a partner.
lessons.main_activity: Children create a self-portrait using paper shapes, wool (for hair) and craft materials, gluing purposefully to represent eyes, nose, mouth, hair.
key_questions: What colour are your eyes?
What shape is your face?

differentiation.support: Pre-cut shapes provided
differentiation.extension: Child cuts own shapes and adds detail (freckles, glasses)

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe fine motor control with glue/scissors and purposeful material choice — evidence for EAD.1 and PD.2.
lessons.plenary: Display portraits on the 'Welcome to Our Class' board; children name one friend's portrait.
lessons.home_link: Talk about family members' faces and what makes everyone unique.

lessons.title: Making a New Friend
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to introduce themselves and ask a friend's name.
lessons.starter_activity: Name game: pass a ball around the circle saying 'Hello, my name is ___.'
lessons.main_activity: Paired activity: children find a partner, ask each other's name and one favourite thing, then feed back one fact about their partner to the group.
key_questions: What is your friend's name?
What did you find out about them?

differentiation.support: Adult models the question and sentence for the child to repeat
differentiation.extension: Child asks a follow-up question independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Note confidence in initiating interaction — evidence for PSED.3.
lessons.plenary: Create a class 'Friendship Chain' paper link with each child's name.
lessons.home_link: Tell someone at home the name of a new friend you made.

lessons.title: Show and Tell: My Favourite Thing
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to speak in a full sentence about a familiar object.
lessons.starter_activity: Adult models Show and Tell with their own object.
lessons.main_activity: Children bring/describe a favourite toy or picture, using the sentence starter 'This is my ___. I like it because ___.'
resources_needed: Children's own items (or drawing if none brought)
key_questions: Why is it special to you?
Can you tell us more about it?

differentiation.support: Adult scribes/prompts each part of the sentence
differentiation.extension: Child answers 2-3 follow-up questions from peers

lessons.assessment_notes: Record use of full sentences vs single words — evidence for CL.2.
lessons.plenary: Vote on class favourite type of item shared (toys vs books vs pictures).
lessons.home_link: Practise describing a favourite object in a full sentence.

lessons.title: Pencil Grip and Mark-Making
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to hold a pencil using an appropriate grip and make controlled marks.
lessons.starter_activity: Finger warm-up rhyme ('Where is Thumbkin?') and playdough squeezing.
lessons.main_activity: Practise tripod grip with large crayons; make lines, circles and zig-zags on large paper following adult demonstration.
key_questions: Can you make a big circle? A wiggly line?
Show me how you hold your pencil.

differentiation.support: Use tripod grip aids/pencil grippers
differentiation.extension: Attempt name-writing with correct letter formation

lessons.assessment_notes: Record pencil grip type observed for each child — evidence for PD.2.
lessons.plenary: Children show their favourite mark they made.
lessons.home_link: Practise holding crayons correctly while colouring at home.

lessons.title: Story Time: 'Starting School' by Janet Ahlberg
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer a simple 'how' or 'why' question about the story.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at front cover and predict what the story is about.
lessons.main_activity: Read the story aloud with expression, pausing to ask prediction and comprehension questions.
resources_needed: Copy of 'Starting School' or similar first-day-of-school story
key_questions: Why do you think the character felt nervous?
How did they feel by the end of the story?

differentiation.support: Use picture prompts to answer with pointing/single words
differentiation.extension: Retell part of the story in own words

lessons.assessment_notes: Note who can answer 'why' questions with reasoning — evidence for LIT.1/CL.1.
lessons.plenary: Compare the story to children's own first day at school.
lessons.home_link: Share a book together and ask one 'why' question about it.

lessons.title: Subitising: Spot the Number Without Counting
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to instantly recognise quantities of 1-3 without counting.
lessons.starter_activity: Flash dot-pattern cards (1-3 dots) briefly and ask 'How many, quick!'
lessons.main_activity: Children play a matching game pairing dot patterns/dice faces to numeral cards for 1-3 (extending to 5 for confident children).
key_questions: How did you know without counting?
Can you show me 3 fingers straight away?

differentiation.support: Limit to 1-2 only
differentiation.extension: Extend subitising to 4-5 and irregular arrangements

lessons.assessment_notes: Record which quantities each child can subitise instantly — evidence for MATHS.1.
lessons.plenary: Quick-fire subitising quiz as a whole class using fingers.
lessons.home_link: Practise showing quick number amounts with fingers at home.

lessons.title: All About My Family
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to talk about members of their own family.
lessons.starter_activity: Adult shares a photo of their own family and describes it.
lessons.main_activity: Children draw their family and label/talk about each member with adult support, discussing similarities and differences between families in the class.
key_questions: Who is in your family?
Are all families the same?

differentiation.support: Adult scribes names next to drawings
differentiation.extension: Child attempts to write family members' names independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding that families vary — evidence for UTW.1/UTW.2.
lessons.plenary: Create a 'Our Families' display wall with all drawings.
lessons.home_link: Bring in a family photo to share (optional, sensitive to family circumstances).

lessons.title: Role-Play: Our New Classroom Café
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to take on a role and use imaginative language during play.
lessons.starter_activity: Adult models being a customer/waiter in the role-play area.
lessons.main_activity: Children take turns as customer and café worker, using play food, taking orders, and using polite imaginative language.
resources_needed: Role-play café area, play food, menus, notepad
key_questions: What would you like to order?
What is your café called?

differentiation.support: Adult joins play to model language
differentiation.extension: Child invents new menu items and prices

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe imaginative language and turn-taking — evidence for EAD.2/PSED.3.
lessons.plenary: Children share their favourite pretend order from the café.
lessons.home_link: Play pretend café/shop at home with family.

lessons.title: Our Classroom Rules
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to explain why one classroom rule is important.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss: 'What makes our classroom a happy place?'
lessons.main_activity: As a group, agree 3-4 simple class rules (e.g. kind hands, listening ears, walking feet). Children illustrate one rule each for a class rules poster.
key_questions: Why do we need this rule?
What happens if we don't follow it?

differentiation.support: Adult gives the reason, child repeats
differentiation.extension: Child gives own reason unprompted

lessons.assessment_notes: Note who can give a reason (not just recall the rule) — evidence for PSED.2.
lessons.plenary: Display and 'sign' the class rules poster together.
lessons.home_link: Talk about family rules at home and why they matter.

lessons.title: Following 2-3 Step Instructions: Obstacle Course
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to follow and carry out a sequence of 2-3 instructions.
lessons.starter_activity: Practise sequencing words with a simple 2-step action (stand up, then sit down).
lessons.main_activity: Set up a simple indoor obstacle course; give instructions in sequence ('crawl under the table, then jump over the hoop, then touch the wall') and children carry them out.
resources_needed: Table, hoops, cushions for obstacle course
key_questions: What do you do first? What comes next?
Can you tell your friend the instructions?

differentiation.support: Give 1 instruction at a time
differentiation.extension: Give 3-step instructions and ask child to repeat them back first

lessons.assessment_notes: Record how many steps each child can hold and execute — evidence for CL.1.
lessons.plenary: Children take turns giving an instruction to the group.
lessons.home_link: Give your child 2-step instructions for a simple chore.

lessons.title: Balancing and Climbing
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to balance while walking along a low beam/line with control.
lessons.starter_activity: Balance on one foot for a count of 5 as a warm-up.
lessons.main_activity: Set up a balance beam (or taped line) and low climbing equipment; children practise walking along with arms out for balance, then attempt simple climbing apparatus with adult supervision.
key_questions: What helps you stay balanced?
How did it feel when you wobbled?

differentiation.support: Hold an adult's hand while balancing
differentiation.extension: Balance while carrying a beanbag or walking backwards

lessons.assessment_notes: Record balance/coordination level — evidence for PD.1.
lessons.plenary: Cool down stretches; children reflect on what was tricky.
lessons.home_link: Practise walking along a line/kerb (with supervision) at home.

lessons.title: Phonics: Introducing 'a'
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to say the sound 'a' and blend it with 's' (as, sa).
lessons.starter_activity: Recap 's' sound from Monday with the action.
lessons.main_activity: Introduce 'a' sound and action. Practise oral blending of two sounds already taught (s-a) with adult modelling, using Fred Talk/robot-arms style blending.
key_questions: What sound is this?
What do we get when we put 's' and 'a' together?

differentiation.support: Practise 'a' sound in isolation only
differentiation.extension: Attempt oral blending of s-a-t (if 't' pre-taught) or similar

lessons.assessment_notes: Update phonics tracker for 'a' sound recognition and blending attempt.
lessons.plenary: Sing the phonics sounds learned so far (s, a) with actions.
lessons.home_link: Practise the 's' and 'a' sounds and actions together.

lessons.title: Comparing Sizes: Big and Small
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to compare two objects and identify which is bigger/smaller.
lessons.starter_activity: Sort a basket of big and small toys into two hoops.
lessons.main_activity: In pairs, children compare classroom objects (e.g. two books, two shoes) and say which is bigger/smaller, then order 3 objects from smallest to biggest.
resources_needed: Assorted classroom objects of varying sizes
key_questions: Which one is bigger? How do you know?
Can you find something smaller than this?

differentiation.support: Compare only 2 objects with clear size difference
differentiation.extension: Order 4-5 objects by size

lessons.assessment_notes: Note accurate use of comparative vocabulary — evidence for MATHS.2.
lessons.plenary: Line up children by height (sensitively) as a size-ordering example.
lessons.home_link: Compare sizes of household objects together (e.g. cups, shoes).

lessons.title: Exploring Our Outdoor Area
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to make a simple observation about the natural environment.
lessons.starter_activity: Look out of the window and predict what we might find outside.
lessons.main_activity: Outdoor walk around the school grounds; children collect/observe natural objects (leaves, stones, twigs) and describe what they notice using magnifying glasses.
key_questions: What can you see/feel/smell?
Is it the same as this other leaf?

differentiation.support: Adult points out objects to observe
differentiation.extension: Child sorts collected items by their own chosen criteria

lessons.assessment_notes: Note quality/detail of observations — evidence for UTW.3.
lessons.plenary: Share one interesting find with the group and add to a nature table.
lessons.home_link: Go on a mini nature walk and collect one interesting object.

lessons.title: Action Songs and Rhymes
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to join in with actions and words of a familiar rhyme.
lessons.starter_activity: Sing a very familiar nursery rhyme together (e.g. 'Twinkle Twinkle').
lessons.main_activity: Teach a new action rhyme (e.g. 'Heads, Shoulders, Knees and Toes'); repeat with increasing speed and encourage children to invent a new verse/action.
key_questions: Can you think of a new action to add?
What happens when we sing it faster?

differentiation.support: Focus on actions only, humming along
differentiation.extension: Invent and lead a new verse for the group

lessons.assessment_notes: Note participation and confidence performing in a group — evidence for EAD.2.
lessons.plenary: Vote on favourite rhyme of the day to sing again.
lessons.home_link: Teach a family member the new rhyme and actions.

lessons.title: Calm Down Strategies
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to name and try one simple strategy to calm down when upset.
lessons.starter_activity: Practise 'balloon breathing' (slow breath in, slow breath out) together.
lessons.main_activity: Introduce a simple 'calm down corner' with visual strategy cards (breathing, counting to 5, squeezing a soft toy). Role-play a scenario where a puppet is upset and children suggest a strategy.
key_questions: What could help the puppet feel calmer?
What helps you feel calm?

differentiation.support: Adult chooses and models one strategy with the child
differentiation.extension: Child suggests more than one strategy and explains preference

lessons.assessment_notes: Note emerging self-regulation vocabulary and strategy use — evidence for PSED.1.
lessons.plenary: Practise the breathing strategy together once more before moving on.
lessons.home_link: Try 'balloon breathing' together if your child feels upset at home.

lessons.title: Retelling a Simple Story Using Puppets
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to retell the main events of a familiar story in order.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap Tuesday's story ('Starting School') using picture cards.
lessons.main_activity: Using simple puppets/props, children retell the story in small groups with adult support using sequencing vocabulary (first, then, next, finally).
key_questions: What happened first? What happened next?
How did the story end?

differentiation.support: Adult sequences 3 picture cards, child names each
differentiation.extension: Child retells independently without prompts

lessons.assessment_notes: Note use of sequencing language and narrative structure — evidence for CL.2/LIT.1.
lessons.plenary: One group performs their retelling to the class.
lessons.home_link: Retell a favourite story to a family member at home.

lessons.title: Scissor Skills
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to hold scissors correctly and cut along a straight line.
lessons.starter_activity: Practise 'open, shut' scissor hand movements in the air (no scissors).
lessons.main_activity: Using safety scissors, children practise snipping fringes on paper, then attempt cutting along a thick straight line.
resources_needed: strips of paper with thick lines
key_questions: Which hand holds the scissors? Which hand holds the paper?
Can you cut along the line?

differentiation.support: Practise snipping only (no line-following)
differentiation.extension: Cut along a curved line or simple shape

lessons.assessment_notes: Record scissor grip and control — evidence for PD.2.
lessons.plenary: Children display their cut strips on the craft table.
lessons.home_link: Practise cutting with child-safe scissors under supervision.

lessons.title: Writing My Name
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to attempt to write the first letter (or more) of their name.
lessons.starter_activity: Find your name card among a pile and match it to your peg/tray.
lessons.main_activity: Trace over own name using a name card as a model, then attempt to write independently on whiteboards, focusing on correct letter formation of the first letter.
key_questions: What is the first letter of your name?
Can you find your name on this list?

differentiation.support: Trace over dotted name outline
differentiation.extension: Write full name independently with correct formation

lessons.assessment_notes: Record name-writing stage (scribble/first letter/full name) — evidence for LIT.3.
lessons.plenary: Children display their name attempt on the 'Look Who's Here!' board.
lessons.home_link: Practise writing your name together at home.

lessons.title: Number Hunt: Finding Numerals Around the Room
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to recognise and name numerals 1-5.
lessons.starter_activity: Sing a counting number song (e.g. '1, 2, 3, 4, 5, Once I Caught a Fish Alive').
lessons.main_activity: Hide numeral cards 1-5 around the classroom; children go on a 'number hunt', find a card, and match it to the corresponding number of objects on a chart.
key_questions: What number did you find?
How many dots match this number?

differentiation.support: Hunt for numerals 1-3 only
differentiation.extension: Extend hunt to numerals up to 10

lessons.assessment_notes: Record numeral recognition range per child — evidence for MATHS.1.
lessons.plenary: Order all found numerals correctly as a class on the floor.
lessons.home_link: Spot numbers around the house (on a clock, remote, etc.) and name them.

lessons.title: My Life So Far: Baby to Now
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to sequence simple events from their own past.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at a baby photo of the teacher and guess who it is.
lessons.main_activity: Children (if photos available) or through discussion sequence pictures/statements of 'When I was a baby...', 'Now I can...' using simple before/after language.
key_questions: What could you do as a baby that's different from now?
What can you do now that you couldn't before?

differentiation.support: Adult provides sentence frames to complete
differentiation.extension: Child sequences 3+ life stages independently

lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of past vs present — evidence for UTW.1.
lessons.plenary: Share one 'I used to... but now I can...' sentence each.
lessons.home_link: Look at a baby photo together and talk about how much you've grown.

lessons.title: Junk Modelling: Build Something New
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to join materials together to create a simple model.
lessons.starter_activity: Look at examples of junk models for inspiration (robot, car, castle).
lessons.main_activity: Using recycled boxes/tubes, children choose materials and join them (tape, glue) to build their own free-choice model.
key_questions: What are you building?
How will you join these two pieces together?

differentiation.support: Adult supports joining technique
differentiation.extension: Child plans model verbally before building

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe problem-solving and joining technique — evidence for EAD.1.
lessons.plenary: Models displayed and children describe what they made.
lessons.home_link: Build something together using recycling at home.

lessons.title: Being a Good Friend: Sharing and Taking Turns
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to take turns during a game without adult reminders (with some support).
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss: 'What does a good friend do?'
lessons.main_activity: Play a simple turn-taking board/floor game in small groups; adult observes and gently reinforces waiting and sharing language.
resources_needed: Simple turn-taking game (e.g. large dice game)
key_questions: Whose turn is it now?
How did it feel to wait for your turn?

differentiation.support: Adult uses a visual turn-taking token/timer
differentiation.extension: Child reminds others whose turn it is

lessons.assessment_notes: Note turn-taking independence — evidence for PSED.1/PSED.3.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate examples of kind sharing seen during the week.
lessons.home_link: Play a turn-taking game together at home.

lessons.title: Show and Tell: My First Week at School
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to talk in sentences about an experience from the week.
lessons.starter_activity: Look back through photos/work from the week on the board.
lessons.main_activity: Circle time: each child completes 'My favourite thing this week was ___ because ___', supported by photo prompts of the week's activities.
key_questions: What was your favourite part of this week?
What is something new you learned?

differentiation.support: Point to a photo and adult scaffolds the sentence
differentiation.extension: Child gives 2-3 sentences with reasoning

lessons.assessment_notes: Compare sentence complexity to Tuesday's Show and Tell — evidence of progress for CL.2.
lessons.plenary: Class cheer/celebration for completing the first week.
lessons.home_link: Tell your family your favourite part of your first week at school.

lessons.title: Team Games: Rolling and Catching
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to roll a ball to a partner with some accuracy and attempt to catch/stop it.
lessons.starter_activity: Warm-up: roll ball to self against a wall.
lessons.main_activity: In pairs, children practise rolling a large soft ball to a partner and stopping/catching it, gradually increasing distance.
key_questions: How do you aim the ball at your friend?
What do your hands do to stop the ball?

differentiation.support: Sit closer together, use a larger ball
differentiation.extension: Increase distance or use a smaller ball

lessons.assessment_notes: Record ball skills progress (rolling accuracy, catching attempts) — evidence for PD.1.
lessons.plenary: Cool down; children reflect on what they found tricky/easy.
lessons.home_link: Practise rolling and catching a ball together outside.

lessons.title: Phonics Review: s, a Recap and Games
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to recall the sounds 's' and 'a' confidently by the end of the week.
lessons.starter_activity: Quick-fire flashcard flip: children say the sound as fast as they can.
lessons.main_activity: Play a phonics matching/lotto game using 's' and 'a' picture and grapheme cards; small groups rotate through phonics stations (sound matching, sand writing, picture sorting).
key_questions: What sound is this letter?
Can you find a picture starting with this sound?

differentiation.support: Focus on one sound at a time with 1:1 support
differentiation.extension: Attempt oral blending s-a with a third known sound if applicable

lessons.assessment_notes: Finalise week 1 phonics tracker entries for every child.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate all sounds learned this week with a sound song.
lessons.home_link: Practice sound flashcards for 's' and 'a' over the weekend.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Counting, Comparing and Numerals
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply counting, comparing and numeral recognition skills learned this week in a game.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap week's key maths vocabulary with actions/props.
lessons.main_activity: Circulate through 3 short maths stations: (1) counting objects into pots, (2) comparing size of two items, (3) matching numeral to dot pattern.
resources_needed: Station resources from the week (counters, size-comparison objects, numeral/dot cards)
key_questions: How many did you count?
Which is bigger?
What number matches this many dots?

differentiation.support: Adult-led rotation with reduced numbers/objects
differentiation.extension: Child self-selects station and records answer on a whiteboard

lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 1 maths observations across all three ELG-linked skills for each child.
lessons.plenary: Class count-along to 10 and back down to celebrate the week.
lessons.home_link: Continue counting everyday objects together over the weekend.

lessons.title: Our Class Community
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to describe one way they are similar to and one way they are different from a classmate.
lessons.starter_activity: Quick survey: 'Stand up if you have a pet / a sibling / like the colour blue' etc.
lessons.main_activity: In pairs, children find one thing they have in common and one thing that is different, then feed back to the group; create a class 'We Are All Different, We Are All the Same' display.
key_questions: What is the same about you and your partner?
What is different?

differentiation.support: Adult prompts comparison with visual cues
differentiation.extension: Child finds more than one similarity/difference

lessons.assessment_notes: Note understanding of similarity/difference concepts — evidence for UTW.2/PSED.3.
lessons.plenary: Admire the completed class community display together.
lessons.home_link: Talk about ways your family is similar to and different from a friend's family.

lessons.title: Celebration Song and Dance: End of Week 1
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to move expressively to music and join in a group performance.
lessons.starter_activity: Free dance warm-up to a favourite class song.
lessons.main_activity: Learn simple movement patterns to a chosen song and perform together as a class 'first week celebration' dance, encouraged to add their own moves.
key_questions: Can you make up your own move?
How does the music make you want to move?

differentiation.support: Copy adult's moves only
differentiation.extension: Lead a move for others to copy

lessons.assessment_notes: Observe expressive movement and confidence performing in a group — evidence for EAD.2.
lessons.plenary: Round of applause for the whole class; recap the fun week they've had.
lessons.home_link: Dance together to a favourite song at home over the weekend.
